transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-08-18 15:00 PDT · 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Mark Donovan (Calypso CTO), Laila Suarez (ML Eng), Ben Carter (Head of Platform)

Summary:
- Quick intro and context: Calypso is building an assistant for traders and a search/QA layer over proprietary docs and trade signals.
- Main decision factors: latency, cost per token, mandatory data residency for EU customers, and support for long context (32k/64k).
- Customer wants to understand open model options, multilingual support, and tool-calling capabilities (we use internal order/quote services).

---
00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, and Priya is our SE who'll run through technicals.
00:12 Priya Patel: Hi all. super quick — can you give the high-level of the workloads? Laila, Mark?
00:20 Mark Donovan: Sure. So primary use is an analyst/trader assistant — chat style plus a vector search augmentation layer over our internal research. second use is a summarization pipeline for compliance (we need redaction before storage). We're looking at high throughput at peak market hours, and some requests need 32k to 64k context to embed whole docs.
00:45 Laila Suarez: And for multilingual: English is 70%, then Spanish and French are next — we want parity across those three for extractive QA and summarization.
01:05 Priya Patel: Great. on the model side — are you leaning open models only, or would you consider closed/hosted models?
01:14 Mark Donovan: We prefer open models for cost and control, but we need to make sure accuracy is good for Spanish/French too. also security: for EU-regulated customers we may need VPC or on-prem options.
01:33 Jordan Lee: Understood. Redwood offers hosted API for fast time-to-value, Dedicated reserved capacity for guaranteed throughput and cost predictability, and Private (VPC or on-prem) for strict residency/compliance. typical tradeoffs: hosted = fastest but shared infra; dedicated = predictable latency & throughput; private = full isolation but longer setup and extra fees.
01:58 Ben Carter: On latency vs cost: during peaks we need sub-500ms for some question-answer flows. is that realistic on dedicated?
02:10 Priya Patel: Sub-500ms is achievable for smaller responses on dedicated with right batching and lower context. For 32k+ contexts latency grows — we'll often use retrieval + short prompt to keep generation low-latency. we can do throughput tuning and kernel selection; but large contexts will increase runtime.
02:40 Mark Donovan: Could you clarify support for tool-calling / function calls? we need the assistant to call our trade-execution service and an internal quoting API.
02:52 Priya Patel: Yes — we support structured function-calling patterns. some open models support this better out-of-the-box; others require light param-parsing layers. Redwood can implement a tool-calling adapter that validates and logs calls; in private setups you can route calls over your internal network for exec.
03:14 Laila Suarez: Any recommended open models for our use-case? long context, good multilingual, cost-conscious.
03:22 Priya Patel: For long context and cost, groups we've seen favor mixed approach: a long-context encoder (e.g., 32k-64k trimmed variants) for retrieval + an LLM for generation. model names — earlier we bench'd Mistral and Mistral-Instruct (some customers report Mistrel spelling hiccups in transcripts), Llama variants, and some new 32k context open-weights. quantized 4-bit variants also cut cost a lot. but watch out for function-calling support; some open models don't have first-class tools.
03:58 Jordan Lee: to add — Redwood provides model catalog and can route to cheaper variants for non-sensitive workloads, or pin higher quality for compliance flows.
04:12 Ben Carter: what's the implication on KV cache and warm-starts? we do a lot of chat sessions and reuse context.
04:20 Priya Patel: KV cache reuse works across sessions if you keep the same conversation id and our runtime supports continuous batching + kv cache management. there's also prefix caching for repeated boilerplate. some terminology in infra docs sometimes comes out as K-V cash in transcripts — but it's KV cache.
04:42 Mark Donovan: For security: we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). and data residency in eu-west-1 for EU customer data.
04:58 Jordan Lee: Redwood supports SOC2; we can provide the report. we have KMS integrations and in Private you can use your own HSM. audit logs and per-route tracing are available in Redwood Console. We'll send our security whitepaper after the call.
05:15 Laila Suarez: For POC, we want a test harness: 1) perf runs with 8k, 32k contexts, 2) multilingual accuracy checks, 3) tool-calling end-to-end. can Redwood run a perf test on our dataset?
05:30 Priya Patel: yes, we can run benchmarks. we'll need a sample dataset and expected query distribution. we'll draft a perf plan — typical runs include 1000 qps bursts and long tail 32k sequences to measure p95/p99 latency and cost per token.
06:00 Mark Donovan: Cost sensitivity — what ballpark for 1B tokens/month on dedicated vs hosted?
06:08 Jordan Lee: we'll share a pricing sheet. ballpark: hosted per-token rates are higher but zero ops; dedicated committed capacity reduces unit cost significantly with reserved GPU pools. exact numbers depend on model, quantization, and batching.
06:26 Ben Carter: Any risk of model regressions when we switch quantized variants? we need quality monitoring.
06:34 Priya Patel: Redwood Optimize helps there — quality monitoring against prompt sets, regression alerts, and rollback/rollout controls. you can A/B between variants and set automatic fallback.
06:50 Mark Donovan: About function-calling: logging and replay for compliance is required. can logs exclude PII?
06:58 Jordan Lee: Yes, we support redaction policies and PII scrubbing in the pipeline before storage; can be configured per-route.
07:15 Laila Suarez: On multilingual fine-tuning — is custom fine-tuning possible on Dedicated/Private?
07:24 Priya Patel: You can run fine-tuning or instruction-tuning pipelines offline. Private deployments let you keep training data inside your VPC. for hosted we have managed fine-tuning with strict controls, but many customers prefer private for regulated datasets.
07:42 Mark Donovan: Ok. I'd like the perf plan to include an 8k and 32k run and a scripted tool-calling flow to our staging quoting API. we'll also want a security deep-dive next week.
07:56 Jordan Lee: Sounds good — our proposed next steps: share security pack & SOC2, send pricing and committed tiers, Priya will share perf plan/runbook, then a follow-up POC scoping call.
08:12 Ben Carter: timeline — we aim to choose vendor by mid-September and start pilot in October. Is that reasonable?
08:20 Jordan Lee: Yes, that's within a normal enterprise timeline for Dedicated/Private onboarding.

(There is occasional crosstalk and filler: ums, ahs, and misattributed words)

22:10 Priya Patel: quick note — for 64k context candidate architectures we sometimes split encoder and generator, the runtime will pick kernels — but that increases complexity and cost.
22:34 Laila Suarez: If we can get acceptable accuracy with 32k, we'd prefer that to 64k because of cost.
23:01 Mark Donovan: we'll send sample docs and the three representative prompt sets by Friday.
23:15 Jordan Lee: I'll send the hosted vs dedicated pricing doc and security whitepaper today/tomorrow. Priya will send perf plan.
23:30 Ben Carter: ok thanks everyone.

Recap / explicit next steps on the call:
- Jordan: Send pricing and security pack (SOC2 report, KMS notes)
- Priya: Share perf benchmark plan and runbook for 8k/32k/64k tests
- Mark: Provide sample prompts, dataset snippets, and expected qps/tokens
- Schedule: follow-up POC scoping call week of 2026-08-24

End of transcript.
